rule_questions: Published-comparison requirement vs comparison_stated=false. Checker brief item 3 says same/contra with no published model-vs-patient comparison should be untested; drafter brief v2 adds comparison_stated as a fact field that must not change the status call, which only makes sense if drafter juxtaposition is allowed. Under the strict reading the efficacy contra (and the safety same) both collapse to untested; under v2 the efficacy contra stands. I scored under v2 and kept contra: Lilly built the trial with TPV as the a-priori proof-of-concept gate, i.e. the direct clinical translation of mouse involution, dosed across 25-fold up to the ceiling the human ERalpha window allowed, for 24 weeks, and stopped it for insufficient TPV reduction. The model's own claim was involution at >=10x below the hormone-affecting dose, so the trial tested that joint claim and it failed; the trial could not test exposures above the testosterone threshold, but the model never claimed those were needed. The brief should state which reading governs.

Safety prediction confirmed inside a sponsor-designed window. The mouse prediction is 'no gonadal-hormone effect at 10x the efficacious dose'. In patients the efficacious dose never materialised and the 1-25 mg range was chosen below the healthy-volunteer testosterone EC50 from Hu 2015, so the clean hormone profile confirms Hu 2015's human PK/PD window under chronic dosing, not the mouse. I propose untested; one could argue the joint 10x-margin claim was contradicted (hormone threshold reached in humans with no efficacy beneath it), but that is the efficacy failure restated and should not be double-counted in safety. The brief does not say how to score a prediction whose reference point (an efficacious dose) was never reached, or one confirmed only inside a window the sponsor designed from human data.

Model-change entries without a status change. The brief says 'one entry per change of status' and rule 6 opens each cell at the first year the (best) model was used; it does not permit a second untested entry when only the model changes. The draft has two such pairs (engagement 2001 BERKO -> 2010 xenograft; efficacy 2001 BERKO -> 2006 CD-1 mouse). Recommendation: efficacy keep 2006 Norman (the model Lilly relied on and the one the 2015 contra is scored against), drop 2001 Weihua into the judgement text; engagement keep 2010 McPherson (a dosed class proxy with a readout a patient study could have matched), drop 2001 Weihua. If the house-style context files (not read here) do allow model-change entries, keep all four and ignore this item. Note the trade-off: dropping the 2001 entries moves model_first_use_year from 2001 to 2006/2010 and shortens the 'model existed before it was tested' strip.
